question: Founders who kept their day job while starting a business, compared with those who quit to do it: what was their failure risk?
answer: About a third lower. Raffiee and Feng followed US founders and found that those who kept their jobs while starting out were about 33% less likely to fail. Part of the gap is who chooses this path: more cautious people. Keeping an income bought time to test the idea before betting everything on it.
move: Test a big bet while something steady pays the bills.
ask: What idea could I test in evenings and weekends before deciding whether to leap?
trap: Stories of all-in founders make half-measures seem doomed.
source: Raffiee and Feng, Academy of Management Journal, 2014
reference: Raffiee and Feng, Should I Quit My Day Job? A Hybrid Path to Entrepreneurship, Academy of Management Journal, 2014
